efficiency.certificateTitle: Net calorific value, weather-adjusted, based on {area} m² usable floor area. A consumption certificate requires 36 months; available: {months}.

welcome.title: Welcome to Energietracker
welcome.text: Enter your meter readings — the app turns them into consumption, costs, advance-payment balance and forecast. Or first see what that looks like with sample data.

readingsEntry.title: Meter readings
readingsEntry.subtitle: Quick on-site entry — all meters at a glance.

error.title: Loading failed
error.invalidNumber: Please enter a number, for example 12345.6.

empty.title: No meters
empty.text: Central entry is only available for cumulative meters (gas, electricity, water, district heating). Heating oil/pellets track consumption via deliveries, not meter readings.

hint.lower: Note: value is lower than the last reading ({min}). That's fine for a meter swap etc.

held.one: {count} reading not saved – please check the marked card.
held.other: {count} readings not saved – please check the marked cards.

noMeters.title: No meters yet
noMeters.text: Add a {label} meter via the meter management.

balance.title: ⚖️ Balance current contract — {name}
balance.subUnderpaid: Additional payment — paid too little so far
balance.subOverpaid: Credit — paid too much so far
balance.suggestAdvance: With an advance of {suggested} instead of {current}, the bill would come out at about ±0.
balance.measuredThenEstimated: measured up to {date} ({kwh} kWh), estimated since: {value}
balance.renewed: The term ended on {date}. Without cancellation the contract runs on at its last prices and can be cancelled any time with at most one month’s notice.
balance.cancelMissed: Cancellation deadline {date} missed: the contract does not end on {end} but runs on — after that it can be cancelled with at most one month’s notice.
balance.priceIncreaseDe: Until then you have a special right to cancel effective on the day of the increase (§ 41 (5) EnWG).

contractsTable.emptyText: Add a contract to track advances, tariff prices, bonuses and balance.
contractsTable.hint: Bonus = credits from the contract (instant, switching, new-customer bonus). Special payments = refunds (+), back-payments and extra advance payments (−) outside the advance schedule; both feed into the balance. Tap to see the individual items; they are maintained in the contract management.

monthlyTable.estimatedTitle: {days} days estimated (after the last known stock)
monthlyTable.estimatedLegend: ≈ month contains estimated days — after the last known stock (delivery “filled to full” or tank reading).

readingsTable.emptyYearHint: {count} readings are recorded in total — reachable via the year selector above.
readingsTable.suspectTitle: Lower than the previous reading (Home Assistant). Counts in the analysis only after confirmation.

tank.noCapacity: No tank capacity set — enter it on the meter to see the stock curve.
tank.noteMeasured: Consumption calculated from known stock levels up to {date}, estimated afterwards.
tank.noteEstimated: Stock and consumption are estimated from the initial stock and the deliveries. A delivery “filled to full” or a tank reading makes them exact.
tank.warnInconsistent: Between {from} and {to} the levels do not add up: {excess} {unit} more in the tank than can be there. Is a delivery missing, or is a level wrong?
tank.warnExhausted: By calculation the tank has been empty since {date}. Is a delivery or a tank reading missing?
tank.warnNoCalibration: No consumption rate yet: it needs two known tank levels at least 14 days apart (initial stock, delivery “Filled to full”, tank reading) or two deliveries.
tank.warnFlat: Temperatures are available for fewer than half of the days — consumption is spread evenly.
tank.levelsEmpty: No tank reading yet. A reading makes the calculation exact up to that day.
tank.levelHint: Read from the tank gauge, a dipstick or a level sensor.
tank.levelRange: Please enter a level between 0 and {cap} {unit}.

chart.alt: Bar chart: monthly consumption and average temperature

readingModal.confirmLower: This reading is below the last one ({last} {unit}). Meter readings normally only go up; a replaced meter belongs under “Meter swap”. Save anyway?

deliveryModal.validation: Date and a positive quantity are required.
deliveryModal.fillToFullHint: The tank was full afterwards. The app then knows the stock on that day and calculates the consumption up to it exactly.

toast.readingConfirmed: Reading confirmed – it now counts in the analysis.

billCheck.title: Bill verification
billCheck.hint: Recalculates the gas bill: per section m³ × volume correction factor × calorific value = kWh, like the lines of a supplier bill. A new section starts at every reading and every calorific-value change.
billCheck.empty: No sections in the chosen range.
billCheck.formula: kWh = m³ × volume correction factor × calorific value. The supplier estimates intermediate readings at calorific-value boundaries; here the reading interval is split day-exactly.
billCheck.errRange: Please choose a valid range (from before to).

kind.interpolated: substitute value — no meter reading on this day, interpolated day-exact between the enclosing readings

billCheck.legend: Reading type: no suffix = meter reading · S = reading recorded as estimated · E = substitute value: there is no meter reading on this day, it is interpolated day-exact between the enclosing readings — exactly where the supplier estimates too (calorific-value and period boundaries). The fewer rows with E, the less is estimation.

gapsN.one: {count} section without an enclosing reading — consumption is missing there.
gapsN.other: {count} sections without an enclosing reading — consumption is missing there.

warnings.title: Implausible meter readings: {count}
warnings.hint: These readings do not count in the analysis or cause a decrease. Correct them, confirm them or record a meter swap.
warnings.suspect: {date}: {counter} {unit} – from Home Assistant, lower than the previous reading; awaiting confirmation
warnings.decrease: {date}: {counter} {unit} – lower than on {prevDate} ({prevCounter} {unit}); meter swap or rollover not recorded?

noData.title: No monthly values yet
noData.noReading: This meter has no reading yet. Monthly values come from the difference between two readings.
noData.oneReading: There is only one reading so far. Monthly values come from the difference between two readings — add a second one, such as the one from your last bill.

contracts.title: {label} · Contracts

delivery.bannerText: Unlike gas, electricity, water or district heating, there is no supply contract with unit prices and standing charges here. Costs come directly from each delivery/tank invoice (quantity × price per {unit}, or the recorded total amount). A tariff comparison with shadow contracts also does not apply to {label}.

contracts.metersWarning: Add meters first before creating contracts.

card.shadowHint: Shadow contract — a what-if scenario for the tariff comparison only. Not counted in costs, balance or forecast.

row.copyStartTitle: Set this row’s date to the contract start
row.setStartFirst: Please set the contract start date first

modal.validationHalfRows: Please complete or clear half-empty rows
modal.noticePeriodHint: The tariff comparison derives the cancellation date from this and warns before the deadline passes.
modal.priceGuaranteeHint: Beyond that the price is an assumption.
modal.minTermEndHint: Only needed for open-ended contracts — no cancellation is possible before this date.
modal.nameRequired: Please enter a provider or tariff.
modal.workingPriceRequired: At least one “{group}” row with date and amount is required.
modal.supersedeMessage: From {date} this contract applies instead of “{name}” – where contracts overlap, the later start wins. Balance and forecast then use the new prices.

noticeModeOption.term_end: at the end of the term

modal.noticeModeHint: Automatic: at the end of the term; without an end, any time at month end. Default supply (Grundversorgung), for example, can be cancelled any time with two weeks’ notice.
modal.autoRenewsHint: After the end the contract runs on at its last prices until it is cancelled — then with at most one month’s notice. Clear this once you have cancelled.

delete.title: Delete contract?
delete.messageNamed: Delete the contract “{name}” permanently? Its prices, advance payments and bonuses are lost.

special.title: Special payments
special.hint: Refund, back-payment or additional advance payment. “Affecting” also adjusts the future monthly advance.

perM3.toggleTitle: Convert a price per m³ to {minor}/kWh
perM3.label: Price per m³ ({cur})

info.title: Multiple meters per utility
info.text: — e.g. hot water & heating (gas) or peak/off-peak & wallbox (electricity). Each meter has its own device history (meter swaps are calculated without loss) and can carry its own contracts.
info.topologyText: Sub-meters are subtracted from the parent meter; groups combine several meters in the dashboard.

deleteGroup.title: Dissolve group?
deleteGroup.message: Dissolve group “{name}”? The assigned meters are kept and are only removed from the group.

deleteMeter.title: Delete meter?
deleteMeter.message: Delete meter “{name}” and its device history? Readings and contracts must be removed first.

modal.name: Name *
modal.namePlaceholder: e.g. hot water, heating, peak, wallbox
modal.parentHint: This meter's consumption is subtracted from the parent meter.
modal.digitsHint: Only needed if the register can roll over from 99999 to 0: the analysis then recognises the rollover instead of reporting a decrease. Empty = unknown.
modal.activeHint: Clear this when the meter is out of service: its history still counts in every total, but it no longer appears in the reading entry and raises no warnings.
modal.initialStockPriceHint: Leave empty to use the price of the first delivery.
modal.heatSourceHint: This electricity meter measures the heating: it counts towards the efficiency figure.

replace.title: Meter swap: {name}
replace.intro: Closes the currently open device with a final reading and creates a new device. Consumption across the swap is calculated correctly automatically — no more “negative consumption” after a swap.
replace.confirmLower: The final reading {oldFinal} {unit} is below the last reading ({last} {unit} on {lastDate}). A meter reading does not go down – please check. Continue anyway?
replace.confirmSummary: On {date} the old device is closed at {oldFinal} {unit} and the new one starts at {newInitial} {unit}. This cannot be undone in the app.

import.title: Import readings: {name}
import.intro: Reads readings from a CSV file for the meter {name}. Before importing, a preview shows every row and what it will do — an existing reading on the same day is replaced.
import.formatHint: Separator ; or , · date DD.MM.YYYY or YYYY-MM-DD · decimal comma allowed · columns note and estimated optional · a header row is detected automatically.
import.dropZone: Drop a CSV file here or click to select
import.dropZoneAria: Select a CSV file or drop it here
import.previewSummary: Read: {rows} · new: {new} · replaces existing: {overwrite} · unchanged: {same} · with notes: {flagged}

otherMeterRows.one: {count} row belongs to another meter and is skipped.
otherMeterRows.other: {count} rows belong to other meters and are skipped.

import.duplicate: Date appears more than once in the file — the last row wins
import.nothing: The file contains no readable row.

mergeModal.title: Group meters
mergeModal.intro: Combine several meters into a group — e.g. off-peak + peak electricity or several wallboxes. The group shows the total on the overview; the meters themselves stay separate and unchanged.
mergeModal.needTwo: Please select at least two meters
mergeModal.needName: Please provide a group name or choose an existing group

baseline.title: Baseline dates
baseline.hint: After building work the house consumes differently for good. Enter the date here — the analyses then start from that point, while older months stay visible but no longer feed the model. A future date may be recorded in advance; it only takes effect once reached.
baseline.label: Description
baseline.none: No baseline date recorded — every analysis uses the full history.
baseline.dateRequired: Please give a date for the baseline

settings.title: Settings

lang.title: 🌐 Language & country / Sprache
lang.hint: Language and country take effect immediately. The country sets number and date formats, currency and time zone; when you change it, the app suggests matching defaults.
lang.label: Language

physical.title: Physical constants
physical.hint: Conversion and heating-degree-day base — affect all analyses.

co2.title: CO₂ emission factors
co2.hint: Grams of CO₂ per consumption unit, for the emission estimate.

billing.title: Billing cycle
billing.hint: Annual settlement date per utility (format DD-MM, e.g. 01-01 for 1 January, 15-04 for 15 April). Determines how far the balance of open contracts is projected; contracts with a maintained end date still use that end.

contractReminders.title: Reminders
contractReminders.hint: Three levels before a contract ends or its notice deadline; for reminders the advance warning and the grace period until “overdue”.

water.title: Water reference values
water.hint: Household size, per-capita reference and the bands of the saving index.

regression.title: Regression & forecast
regression.hint: Filters for the regression basis and parameters of the forecast model.

dashboard.title: Display
dashboard.hint: Time span of the overview and the forecast; when a missing reading is flagged.

building.title: Building & efficiency
building.hint: Reference values for the efficiency class (kWh/m²·a) and the heating-energy benchmark.

delivery.title: Energy sources (delivery)
delivery.hint: Energy content of delivery-based fuels and the tank warning threshold.

remindersRec.title: Recommendations & distribution
remindersRec.hint: Thresholds of the recommendations and the base-load share used to spread heating oil and pellets over the days.

location.title: Location (Open-Meteo)
location.hint: Coordinates for the weather sync of the temperature series.

embedding.title: Embedding
embedding.hint: Other sites may not embed Energietracker – this protects against hijacked clicks. For a webpage card on a Home Assistant dashboard, enter its address here.

hdd_base_temp.label: HDD base temperature
hdd_base_temp.hint: Heating limit — days below count as heating days.

co2_gas.label: CO₂ gas
co2_gas.hint: BAFA: 201 g/kWh, based on the net calorific value. The app counts gas by gross calorific value (z-number × calorific value), hence × 0.906 = 182.

co2_strom.label: CO₂ electricity
co2_strom.hint: Applies to years before the first yearly value — without yearly values, to all years.

co2_wasser.label: CO₂ water
co2_wasser.hint: For treatment and pumping per m³ of water — an estimate without an official source.

co2_fernwaerme.label: CO₂ district heating
co2_fernwaerme.hint: BAFA flat rate. Your heat network’s own value is more accurate — ask your supplier.

co2_heizoel.label: CO₂ heating oil
co2_heizoel.hint: BAFA, based on the net calorific value — as the app calculates heating oil.

co2_pellets.label: CO₂ pellets
co2_pellets.hint: BAFA, CO₂ equivalents including the upstream chain.

wasser_personen_anzahl.label: People in household
wasser_personen_anzahl.hint: For the water saving index: litres per person and day compared with the reference.

wasser_personen_referenz.label: Reference
wasser_personen_referenz.hint: BDEW 2024: 122 L per person and day (Germany).

wasser_sparindex_gut.label: Saving index — good up to
wasser_sparindex_gut.hint: Index ≤ this value is considered unremarkable.

wasser_sparindex_warnung.label: Saving index — warning from
wasser_sparindex_warnung.hint: Index ≥ this value indicates saving potential.

min_days_period.label: Min. days per period
min_days_period.hint: Months with fewer recorded days (partial months) stay out of the heating signature and anomalies.

min_hdd_regression.label: Min. HDD for regression
min_hdd_regression.hint: Months with fewer degree days stay out of the heating signature — in summer the base load drives consumption, not the weather.

blend_max.label: Max. blend weight
blend_max.hint: Highest weight of the weather model in the forecast; the rest comes from the seasonal profile. 0.8 means at least 20 % seasonal profile.

forecast_months.label: Forecast horizon
forecast_months.hint: How many months the forecast looks ahead (1–24). Default of the forecast view.

forecast_model.label: Default model
forecast_model.hint: Model for forecast and tariff comparison. Linear suits most homes; the analysis shows which one explains your data best.

segmented_split_mode.label: Segment breakpoint
segmented_split_mode.hint: auto = fitted from data, fixed = fixed HDD value below.

anomaly_threshold.label: Anomaly threshold
anomaly_threshold.hint: From what deviation (in units of spread σ) a month counts as unusual in the analysis. Smaller means more sensitive.

dashboard_months.label: Months on dashboard
dashboard_months.hint: How many months the history on the overview shows (3–36).

alert_days_since_reading.label: Warn after
alert_days_since_reading.hint: If the last reading is older, the meter appears under “To do” and the consumption view reminds you.

wohnflaeche_m2.label: Living area
wohnflaeche_m2.hint: Heated area — denominator of the efficiency metric.

gebaeudetyp.label: Building type
gebaeudetyp.hint: Multi-family means three or more flats.

heizoel_kwh_per_l.label: Heating oil energy content
heizoel_kwh_per_l.hint: Energy per litre of heating oil (net calorific value, usually 10 kWh/L). Converts litres to kWh.

pellets_kwh_per_kg.label: Pellets energy content
pellets_kwh_per_kg.hint: Energy per kg of pellets (usually 4.8 kWh/kg). Converts kg to kWh.

delivery_baseload_share.label: Base-load share distribution
delivery_baseload_share.hint: Share of consumption as weather-independent base load (rest HDD-weighted).

tank_warn_pct.label: Tank warning from
tank_warn_pct.hint: Below this level the tank turns yellow, below half of it red, and “To do” suggests a delivery.

reminder_warn_days_before.label: Reminder “due soon” from
reminder_warn_days_before.hint: From this many days before the date, a reminder counts as “due soon”.

reminder_overdue_days.label: Grace until “overdue”
reminder_overdue_days.hint: For this many days after the date a reminder still counts as due, then as overdue. 0 = from the next day.

recommendation_anomaly_sigma.label: Recommendation anomaly threshold
recommendation_anomaly_sigma.hint: The same kind of threshold for recommendations: only from this deviation on does a tip appear.

recommendation_trend_pct_year.label: Recommendation trend threshold
recommendation_trend_pct_year.hint: From what increase per year the recommendations report rising consumption.

weather_auto_fill.label: Fill weather automatically
weather_auto_fill.hint: Fetches temperatures from Open-Meteo at most once a day when the app opens (location rounded to about 1 km).

gas_conversion_factors.label: Gas conversion factors
gas_conversion_factors.hint: One entry per calorific-value period, exactly as the gas bill states them: valid from, volume correction factor and calorific value — the kWh/m³ factor is derived. Without a breakdown, enter the factor directly. The undated entry applies to everything before the first effective date. Consumption splits every reading interval day-exactly at the effective dates.

frame_ancestors.label: Allowed embedding addresses
frame_ancestors.hint: Address with scheme and port, e.g. http://homeassistant.local:8123; separate several with spaces. Empty = only this installation itself.

co2_strom_years.label: CO₂ electricity per year
co2_strom_years.hint: Electricity mix per year (German Environment Agency, UBA). After the last year its value applies, before that “CO₂ electricity”.

beheizter_keller.label: Heated basement
beheizter_keller.hint: Single-/two-family or terraced house with heated basement: usable floor area = 1.35 × living area (otherwise 1.2) — for the certificate-style figure.

warmwasser_dezentral.label: Decentralised hot water
warmwasser_dezentral.hint: Hot water from an instantaneous heater or boiler, not from the heating: the certificate-style figure gets a 20 kWh/m²·yr surcharge.

confidence_band_sigma.label: Forecast band width
confidence_band_sigma.hint: In units of spread σ: 1.28 means consumption falls inside the band in 80 % of years; 1.64 would be 90 %.

activeUtils.title: 🧩 Active utilities
activeUtils.hint: Only checked utilities appear in the sidebar, dashboard and annual report. Data of inactive utilities is kept.

pdf.title: 📄 PDF annual report
pdf.hint: Multi-page report with overview, efficiency class, consumption tables per utility and open recommendations.
pdf.moved: The annual report now has its own page under “Insights”.

export.title: 📤 Data export (CSV)
export.hint: Tabular export for Excel, LibreOffice or Google Sheets — semicolon-separated, UTF-8 with BOM, German decimal comma. Complements the full JSON backup below.
export.monthlyHint: Consumption, cost, advance and balance per month.
export.readingsHint: Cumulative types: raw readings. Heating oil/pellets: fuel deliveries (one row per delivery).
export.temperaturesHint: Daily min / avg / max values of the whole series.

backup.title: 💾 Backup & restore
backup.hint: Full JSON backup (format v3.0) — contains all utilities, meters, contracts, temperatures and settings, re-importable.
backup.demoHint: “Load demo data” imports a complete example dataset — ideal for trying out an empty Energietracker. If data already exists, you are warned first and a snapshot is created automatically.
backup.demoUnavailable: Demo data is not available in this installation.
backup.demoConfirmMsg: Data already exists. The import overwrites it. Beforehand, a safety snapshot of your current data is created automatically, which you can restore at any time.
backup.importConfirmMsg: The current data will be overwritten. The app first creates a safety snapshot automatically – you can restore it under “Stored snapshots”.
backup.migrateHint: Upload an old v0.9.0 backup (JSON with version: "2.1"). The backup is analysed before writing; then you choose between Replace (overwrite everything) or Merge (add new IDs only). In both cases a safety snapshot of the current data is created automatically beforehand.
backup.snapshotsHint: Snapshots are kept on the server under data/backups/. Automatic snapshots (before import, migration, demo data) are cleaned up after 30 days, keeping at least three per occasion; of your own, the last ten are kept.
backup.snapRestoreMsg: The snapshot from {date} replaces the current data. The app first saves the current state as a snapshot of its own.
backup.snapDeleteMsg: The snapshot from {date} will be deleted permanently.
backup.previewIntro: The backup is fully readable. It contains:
backup.previewUntouched: Not in the backup – stays unchanged: {list}

problem.counter: meter reading is not a number

ha.title: 🏠 Home Assistant integration
ha.intro: Let Home Assistant send your meter readings to the Energietracker automatically — you no longer maintain them by hand. Home Assistant provides the values, the Energietracker handles contracts, costs and forecasts.
ha.tokenHint: Protects the push endpoint /api/ingest. Without sign-in it also accepts values without a token – meant for the home network. With sign-in switched on, it always requires a token.
ha.revealLabel: Token (copy now — it will not be shown again):
ha.aliasHint: Give each meter an easy-to-remember alias (e.g. electricity_house) that you enter in Home Assistant — more convenient than the internal ID. Allowed: letters, digits, _ . -. Leave empty = no alias.
ha.configHint: Add the REST command to your configuration.yaml and check the URL; put the token entry into secrets.yaml. Templates up to v2.5.2 contained float(0) and recorded a meter reading of 0 whenever the sensor was unavailable – please replace them with this version.
ha.genConfirmMsg: A new token is generated and shown only ONCE. Any existing token becomes invalid.
ha.revokeConfirmMsg: After revoking, the push endpoint is reachable without a token again (open mode). Home Assistant automations with the old token will fail.
ha.automationHint: In the automation editor choose “Edit in YAML” and paste. There is one entry per meter with an alias; set sensor_entity to the entity holding the absolute meter reading. has_value skips a meter whose sensor is currently unavailable.

yaml.floatComment: float without a default: if the sensor is unavailable the push fails instead of recording 0.
yaml.hasValueComment: Only send when the sensor has a value – right after a restart it is briefly “unavailable”.

ha.neverUsed: Nothing has arrived with this token yet.
ha.loginNeedsToken: Sign-in is switched on: without a token, Energietracker accepts no values from Home Assistant.

migrationDialog.title: Migration from v0.9.0
migrationDialog.detected: Detected v0.9.0 backup format {version}. Data has been translated to the current schema (not yet written).
migrationDialog.candidatesHint: — model as device swap after the import?
migrationDialog.candidatesNote: After the import, model them under Meters & devices → Meter swap (or API: POST /api/utility/{u}/meters/{id}/replace-device).
migrationDialog.replaceDesc: — existing data is deleted and replaced by the backup. A safety snapshot of the current data is stored under data/backups/ automatically beforehand.
migrationDialog.mergeDesc: — only readings/contracts with a new ID are added. Existing data is kept. Temperature days are only added if the date does not yet exist.

gasFactors.none: No entry yet — the default factor applies.
gasFactors.errOneUndated: There is already an undated entry — please give a “valid from” date
gasFactors.errDuplicate: There is already an entry for this date
gasFactors.errNeedValues: Please give volume correction factor and calorific value — or the factor directly
gasFactors.mjHint: Calorific values in MJ/m³ or GJ/Smc are converted and stored as kWh/m³ (1 kWh = 3.6 MJ).

countryHint.GB: UK gas bills: enter the volume correction factor 1.02264 and the calorific value in MJ/m³. Imperial meters (ft³) are not supported.
countryHint.IT: Italian gas bills: enter the “coefficiente C” as correction factor and the PCS (gross calorific value), usually in GJ/Smc. The contract form converts prices per Smc to {minor}/kWh.
countryHint.NL: Dutch gas bills: enter the calorific value (calorische waarde) in MJ/m³. The contract form converts prices per m³ to {minor}/kWh.

gasFactors.defaultHint: Default factor 11.5 kWh/m³ active. Your network’s value is on the gas bill (z-number × calorific value) — typically 10.3 to 11.1. With the default, kWh, costs and CO₂ are up to 20 % too high.

settings.invalidFields: Not saved: please correct the fields marked in red.
settings.dayMonthInvalid: Please enter as day-month, e.g. 01-10 for 1 October.

security.title: 🔐 Sign-in & access
security.hint: Without sign-in, anyone who knows the address can reach Energietracker – meant for your own home network. If it is reachable from outside (port forwarding, reverse proxy) or you share the network with others, switch sign-in on.
security.modeFixed: Set by the environment variable ET_AUTH – cannot be changed here.
security.passwordFixed: The password is set by the environment variable ET_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH – cannot be changed here.
security.proxyHint: Sign-in is handled by the upstream proxy (e.g. Authelia or Authentik). Energietracker accepts the user only from the addresses in ET_TRUSTED_PROXIES.
security.enableHint: Each browser then asks for the password once and stays signed in for 30 days. Home Assistant then needs an API token (card “Home Assistant integration”), scripts need an API key.
security.mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
security.enabled: Sign-in switched on. This browser stays signed in.
security.changed: Password changed. Other devices have to sign in again.
security.disableMsg: Energietracker will then be reachable without a password again. Enter the current password to confirm.
security.keysHint: With sign-in switched on, scripts and other programs need a key – as the header Authorization: Bearer etk_…. “Read” may only fetch data, “Manage” may also change it. The Home Assistant push keeps using its own token.
security.keyReveal: Key “{name}” – copy it now, it will not be shown again:
security.keyRevokeMsg: Programs using the key “{name}” will lose access.

region.currencyNote: Amounts are not converted — the currency only changes the symbol and labels.
region.applyIntro: The country profile suggests these values:
region.applyKeep: Meters, contracts and readings stay unchanged; amounts are not converted.

source.ember2024: CO₂ electricity: Ember 2024, generation mix (via Our World in Data)
source.default: CO₂ electricity: the app’s previous default
source.uba: CO₂ electricity: German Environment Agency, electricity mix per year

co2Years.none: No yearly values — “CO₂ electricity” applies to all years.
co2Years.invalid: Please enter a year (1990–2100) and a value between 0 and 2000 g/kWh.

defaultUpdates.title: Newer default values available
defaultUpdates.hint: These values come from an earlier version. They were kept so that no figure changes by itself during the update. The new values have a documented source.
defaultUpdates.sources: Sources: BAFA information sheet on CO₂ factors (2026), German Environment Agency (electricity mix per year), BDEW (water use 2024).

r1.title: {label} {ym}: {pct} % above expectation
r1.detail: In {ym} consumption was {pct} % above what this weather would lead one to expect. An appliance or heating check may be worthwhile.

r2.title: {label}: {pct} % more than the previous year
r2.detail: The last twelve months were {pct} % above the same months of the previous year, weather-adjusted. Check whether appliances are ageing or habits have changed.

r3.title: {label} {year}: high summer consumption
r3.detail: In July {year} consumption was {pct} % of the January value. For pure space heating this should be much lower — likely inefficient hot-water preparation.

r4.title: {label} {ym}: statistical anomaly
r4.detail: Consumption in {ym} is well above what is usual for this month ({sigma}σ). Worth a closer look.

r5.title: {label}: tank at {pct} %
r5.detail: The modelled stock of “{name}” is around {stock} {unit} ({pct} % of capacity). A delivery should be scheduled.

r6.title: {label}: contract ends in {days} days

r6.detailCancel: For the contract “{provider}” to end on {end} instead of running on, the cancellation must reach the supplier by {date}. Start a tariff comparison now and switch if needed.

r7.title: {label}: efficiency class {class} ({kwh} kWh/m²·a)

contractsOverview.subtitle: Current contracts of all utilities: deadlines, advance payments and what to expect at the next bill.
contractsOverview.noUtilities: No utility with contracts is active.

billCheck.noMeter: The bill check recalculates correction factor × calorific value and is therefore available for gas. Set up a gas meter first.

hdd.text: How cold it was, measured against the heating threshold: per day the difference between the threshold and the daily mean, 0 on warm days. More degree days mean more heating demand.

heatingLimit.text: The outdoor temperature below which heating starts — usually 15 °C in Germany (setting “HDD base temperature”). Warmer days count no degree days.

heatingSignature.text: The relation between degree days and consumption, calculated from your own months: how much your home uses per degree day and how large the weather-independent base load is.

baseload.text: The part of consumption that does not depend on the weather — hot water, cooking or standby, for example. It occurs in summer too.

weatherAdjusted.text: Consumption converted to normal weather at your location (climate normal). Only the weather share is converted, so a mild and a cold winter become comparable.

climateNormal.text: Average degree days per calendar month from 30 years of weather data for your location. The basis for forecast and weather adjustment.

r2.text: How well a model explains your monthly values — from 0 (not at all) to 1 (completely). From about 0.7 the relation is clear.

models.text: Linear: a straight line. Polynomial: a slightly curved line. Robust (Huber): like linear, but insensitive to outliers. Segmented: two lines with a break point where heating starts. Sigmoid: an S-curve that flattens in severe cold.

movingAverage.text: The mean of the last 3 or 6 months. It smooths out single outliers and shows the trend.

forecastBlend.text: The forecast blends the weather model with your seasonal profile (average per calendar month). The better the model fits (R²), the more it counts — up to the “Max. blend weight”.

anomaly.text: A month that differs clearly from what was expected for exactly this month. The threshold (σ) says by how many units of spread it must differ at least.

balance.text: The difference between the cost of your consumption and the advance payments made (including one-off payments). Credit: you paid more and get money back. Additional payment: consumption cost more.

advance.text: The monthly payment made in advance to the supplier. The annual bill compares the total with the actual costs.

workingPrice.text: The price per unit consumed — ct/kWh, for water ct/m³.

basePrice.text: A fixed amount per month, independent of consumption.

specialPayment.text: A refund, additional payment or extra advance outside the monthly advance. “With effect” also changes the future advance.

offer.text: A tariff you do not have — from a comparison site, for example. It only affects the tariff comparison, never balance, forecast or contract status. Technically it is a shadow contract.

switchDate.text: The first day a new tariff could supply — from contract end and notice period. The cancellation must reach the supplier by the notice deadline.

noticeDeadline.text: The last day the cancellation must reach the supplier. If missed, a contract that renews unless cancelled is extended.

breakEven.text: The annual volume above which an offer is cheaper than your contract. If it is far from your consumption, the decision holds even with an imprecise forecast. A dash means there is no crossing point: the offer is cheaper or dearer at any volume.

baseline.text: A date from which your home changed — insulation or a new heating system, for example. Evaluations start at the baseline date so old values do not distort the picture.

calorificValue.text: The energy content of one cubic metre of gas in kWh, as the supplier states it per period on the bill.

zNumber.text: Converts the measured gas volume to standard conditions (pressure, temperature). kWh = m³ × correction factor × calorific value.

cutoffDate.text: The day from which a new value applies — a new price or calorific value, for example. Up to the day before, the old one applies.

efficiency.text: Heating energy per m² and year (kWh/m²·yr). The home figure refers to the living area; the certificate-style figure calculates like an energy certificate (net calorific value, weather-adjusted, usable area). Not an official certificate.

feedIn.text: Solar power you deliver to the grid. The remuneration is revenue — more is better here.

selfConsumption.text: Solar power you use yourself: generation minus feed-in. It replaces grid power — the saving is calculated with your unit price.

autarky.text: The share of your electricity consumption covered by your own system.

selfConsumptionRate.text: The share of the solar energy generated that you use yourself.

estimated.text: A reading that was estimated rather than read — often by the supplier. It counts but stays marked.

tankBook.text: For heating oil and pellets, consumption follows from initial stock, deliveries and known stock levels (delivery “to full”, tank reading). Between two known levels it is calculated, afterwards estimated.

subMeter.text: A submeter measures part of another meter and is subtracted from it so that nothing counts twice. A group only combines meters for the overview.

co2Avoided.text: Solar power replaces grid power. The calculation uses the CO₂ factor of grid electricity (Settings → Utilities & billing) — this much CO₂ would otherwise have been emitted. Simplified: manufacturing the system is not included.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.englishOnly: The documentation exists in German and English; the links lead to the English version.

support.title: Questions and bugs
support.text: Questions, requests and bug reports go to the GitHub project. A bug report is easier with the details from the diagnostics under Settings → System.

privacy.title: Your data
privacy.text: Everything stays on your server: no accounts, no ads, no telemetry. The app only talks to Open-Meteo — for the daily weather sync (only the location rounded to about 1 km, can be switched off under Settings → Weather data) and for the place search when you use it.

location.title: Set your location
location.text: The app needs the weather at your location for degree days and forecast.

firstReading.title: Add your first meter reading
firstReading.text: Read your meters and enter the values.

secondReading.title: Add a second reading
secondReading.text: Consumption comes from the difference between two readings — for example, add the reading from your last bill.

contract.title: Add your contract
contract.text: With prices and advance payment the app calculates costs and tells you whether an additional payment is coming.

homeAssistant.title: Connect Home Assistant
homeAssistant.text: Send meter readings automatically instead of typing them.
